# Overview

Physiological responses vary substantially between individuals. 
Models developed from a single participant may capture subject-specific patterns rather than generalizable physiological relationships.

This notebook extends the heart rate feature pipeline across multiple participants in the WESAD dataset.

The goals are:

1. Process multiple ECG recordings
2. Extract heart rate features across participants
3. Create subject-level prediction datasets
4. Evaluate model generalization
5. Investigate individual variability in physiological responses


# Libraries

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(tidymodels)
library(pROC)

processed_files <- list.files(
  here("data", "processed"),
  pattern = "_ecg.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)


processed_files

extract_hr_features <- function(file){

  
  ecg_data <- read_csv(
    file,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )


  subject_id <- basename(file) %>%
    str_remove("_ecg.csv")


  fs <- 700


  # Simple peak detection
  peaks <- pracma::findpeaks(
    ecg_data$ecg,
    minpeakdistance = 350,
    threshold = 0.5
  )


  if(is.null(peaks)){
    return(NULL)
  }


  peak_indices <- peaks[,2]

  peak_times <- ecg_data$time[peak_indices]

  peak_times <- sort(peak_times)


  rr_intervals <- diff(peak_times)


  rr_intervals <- rr_intervals[
    rr_intervals > 0.3 &
    rr_intervals < 2
  ]


  heart_rate <- 60 / rr_intervals


  hr_data <- tibble(
    time = peak_times[2:length(peak_times)][
      1:length(heart_rate)
    ],
    heart_rate = heart_rate
  )


  # Match labels

  hr_data <- hr_data %>%
    mutate(
      label = ecg_data$label[
        findInterval(
          time,
          ecg_data$time
        )
      ]
    )


  # Feature engineering

  features <- hr_data %>%
    mutate(
      window = floor(time / 60)
    ) %>%
    group_by(window) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_hr = mean(heart_rate),
      sd_hr = sd(heart_rate),
      max_hr = max(heart_rate),
      min_hr = min(heart_rate),
      label = first(label),
      subject = subject_id,
      .groups="drop"
    )


  return(features)

}

all_features <- map_dfr(
  processed_files,
  extract_hr_features
)


head(all_features)

model_data <- all_features %>%
  mutate(
    stress = ifelse(
      label == 2,
      "Stress",
      "Non-Stress"
    ),
    stress = factor(stress)
  )


table(model_data$stress)

model_data %>%
  count(subject)

set.seed(123)


subjects <- unique(model_data$subject)


test_subjects <- sample(
  subjects,
  size = floor(length(subjects)*0.25)
)


train_data <- model_data %>%
  filter(
    !subject %in% test_subjects
  )


test_data <- model_data %>%
  filter(
    subject %in% test_subjects
  )


test_subjects

log_model <- logistic_reg() %>%
  set_engine("glm") %>%
  fit(
    stress ~ mean_hr + sd_hr + max_hr + min_hr,
    data=train_data
  )


log_model

predictions <- predict(
  log_model,
  test_data,
  type="prob"
) %>%
  bind_cols(test_data)


head(predictions)

roc_curve <- roc(
  predictions$stress,
  predictions$.pred_Stress
)


auc_value <- auc(
  roc_curve
)


auc_value

plot(
  roc_curve,
  main="Cross-Subject Stress Classification ROC Curve"
)

tidy(
  log_model$fit
)

predictions %>%
  group_by(subject) %>%
  summarise(
    n=n(),
    mean_prediction=mean(.pred_Stress),
    .groups="drop"
  )

write_csv(
  all_features,
  here(
    "data",
    "processed",
    "multisubject_features.csv"
  )
)
```
